review_method: Independent original-map pixel inspection, complete source and baseline-rendered ring plots, registered outline and filled overlays, publication imprints, enlarged northern and southern first-target views and northeastern and southeastern third-target views. All 257 ordered positions across three single-ring Polygons were independently compared with retained source geometry, decoded geometry and exact original inventory/core/detail joins. The Manitoba GeoPDF full embedded affine was independently reopened, including both rotation terms, and every registration recomputed. For the cross-border second target, the retained Saskatchewan WSA original affine and all 40 registrations were independently reopened and recomputed. Both retained successful acquisition receipts were verified against original bytes. Every selected position falls within an inspected original crop; cartographic content is geographically limited inside those crops. Initial observations for each publication were recorded before comparison with separate research findings. Neither bounds nor label overlap alone established identity. The production decoder was not independently replayed by this reviewer.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory lake target IDs; repeated map labels do not increase the target count.

findings.follow_up_scope: Resolve the northern-arm attribution and Highrock/Nelson component partitions before any whole-feature scalar naming. This is a name-scope hold, not an access failure.
findings.supported_name_scope: The single selected ring combines Highrock Lake and Nelson Lake associations, which are non-exhaustive. The northern arm has unresolved named-water scope; proximity to the Suwannee Lake label does not establish a Suwannee component. Western Highrock bays and detailed southern and eastern continuations lie outside the selected ring, while coarse margins cross mapped land. Exact component partitions and complete detailed named-lake extents remain unverified. Exact extent and product-name application are not approved.
limits: The single selected ring combines Highrock Lake and Nelson Lake associations, which are non-exhaustive. The northern arm has unresolved named-water scope; proximity to the Suwannee Lake label does not establish a Suwannee component. Western Highrock bays and detailed southern and eastern continuations lie outside the selected ring, while coarse margins cross mapped land. Exact component partitions and complete detailed named-lake extents remain unverified.

Suwannee Lake is a nearby label, not an established third component or alias. Flatrock Lake lies southwest; Granville Lake, Costello Lake and Laurie River lie north. Geological colors and symbols do not define water-name boundaries.

The retained official Manitoba Geological Survey publication provides the direct water labels. The retained Saskatchewan WSA map provides complementary western shape context only for the border target. Two provincial-government publisher groups are represented; underlying hydrographic dataset independence and formal naming-registry authority are unverified.
No Korean form or whole-feature alias is certified; registered overlays do not establish surveyed shores or exact name partitions.
